newsitem.title: USA: US, EU officials in informal talks on meat trade.
newsitem.headline: US, EU officials in informal talks on meat trade.

text.p: U.S. and European Union officials met informally on Friday to work on overcoming obstacles to an agreement on rules governing trans-Atlantic meat trade.
Talks began in the early afternoon and still were under way about three hours later, a U.S. Agriculture Department spokesman said.
Prospects for an agreement appeared dim before the session began. Four days of discussion earlier in the week had not led to an agreement on the so-called veterinary equivalency issue.
Hundreds of millions of dollars in trade are at stake.
The European Union has said it would implement new veterinary and sanitary controls on April 1. The USDA has said it would retaliate for any curtailment in access to European markets.
"Our government told us flat out there were many stumbling blocks," said one industry official who was briefed Thursday on the negotiations.
A National Broiler Council spokesman said his group would prefer an extension if a deal was not struck, rather than trade being cut off, but it appeared an extension was not being discussed.
The original deadline for agreement was January 1, but the EU allowed an additional 90 days.
